prompt:
A student team conducts a laboratory investigation with a dynamic cart on an inclined track and records the following entries in their experimental log:
Entry 1: Mass of cart = 0.60 kg
Entry 2: Travel time down the track = 1.50 s
Entry 3: Net pulling force = 3.6 N down the ramp
Entry 4: Final kinetic energy = 1.8 J
Entry 5: Final velocity = 2.4 m s^-1

(a)(i) Identify which entry represents an incomplete vector report, and explain what is missing. [2]
(a)(ii) Rewrite the identified entry so that it is a complete and valid vector report. [1]
(b) Classify Entry 1, Entry 2, and Entry 4 as scalar or vector quantities, giving a brief scientific reason for each. [2]
(c) After leaving the ramp, the cart moves in a horizontal circle at a constant speed of 2.4 m s^-1.
Explain why its kinetic energy remains constant while its momentum is continuously changing. [1]

answer.text:
(a)(i) Entry 5 (final velocity) is incomplete because velocity is a vector quantity and its spatial direction is missing.
(a)(ii) Final velocity = 2.4 m s^-1 down the ramp (or in the direction of motion).
(b) Entry 1 (mass), Entry 2 (time), and Entry 4 (kinetic energy) are all scalars because they have magnitude only and do not require or possess a spatial direction.
(c) Kinetic energy is a scalar quantity depending only on mass and the square of speed (magnitude of velocity), which are constant. Momentum is a vector quantity (p = m * v) whose direction changes continuously as the cart moves around the circle.

9702_t01_cm05_l09_theory09_a_ii.solution: Final velocity = 2.4 m s^-1 down the ramp.

hints: Check whether mass, time, or kinetic energy require a direction.
mark_scheme: 1 mark: Reason: each quantity is completely defined by magnitude and unit only / none has direction.
9702_t01_cm05_l09_theory09_b.solution: Entries 1, 2, and 4 are all scalars because mass, time duration, and energy have magnitude only and do not point in any direction.

hints: Distinguish between scalar energy (depends on speed) and vector momentum (depends on velocity).
mark_scheme: 1 mark: Kinetic energy is a scalar depending only on constant speed (magnitude), whereas momentum is a vector whose direction changes as the path curves.
9702_t01_cm05_l09_theory09_c.solution: Kinetic energy is a scalar depending on the square of speed, which is constant. Momentum is a vector (p = m * v), and its direction changes continuously on a circular path.

mark_scheme: (a)(i) [2 marks]: 1 mark for Entry 5; 1 mark for stating that velocity is a vector and lacks direction.
(a)(ii) [1 mark]: Final velocity = 2.4 m s^-1 down the ramp (or forward / in direction of motion).
(b) [2 marks]: 1 mark for identifying all three as scalars; 1 mark for stating that they have magnitude only / no direction.
(c) [1 mark]: Kinetic energy is scalar and speed is constant, while momentum is vector and its direction is continuously changing.
hints: A complete vector report needs magnitude, unit, and direction.
Direction changes in circular motion affect vectors, not scalars.
solution:
(a)(i) Entry 5 lacks direction.
(a)(ii) 2.4 m s^-1 down the ramp.
(b) Entries 1, 2, and 4 are scalars (magnitude only).
(c) Kinetic energy depends on speed (scalar); momentum has direction (vector) which continuously changes.
